headline: OpenAI Confidentially Files S-1 IPO Prospectus with SEC, Targeting Q4 2026 Listing at Up to $1 Trillion
raw_snippet: OpenAI confidentially filed its S-1 IPO prospectus with the SEC on May 22, 2026, targeting a Q4 2026 public listing at a valuation between $852 billion and $1 trillion. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are co-leading the deal, with JPMorgan Chase also involved. The company is generating roughly $2 billion per month in revenue with an annualized run rate of $25 billion, but reported a negative 122% non-GAAP operating margin in Q1 2026. CEO Altman told staff that 'filing is different from being ready to go public.'
curator_notes: Biggest story of the week for IB audience. Clustered 4 sources. CNBC primary for breaking news; Fortune adds governance questions; RoboRhythms adds financial detail (-122% margin, $600B compute commitments); Axios adds competitive context (SpaceX, Anthropic IPO wave).

headline: Jury Unanimously Dismisses All Claims in Musk v. OpenAI Lawsuit on Statute of Limitations
raw_snippet: A nine-member advisory jury in Oakland, California took less than 90 minutes to unanimously dismiss all claims in Elon Musk's lawsuit against Sam Altman, Greg Brockman, and OpenAI, finding that Musk was beyond the three-year statute of limitations when he filed in February 2024. Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers agreed and tossed the case. Musk had alleged the defendants 'stole a charity' and sought up to $150 billion in disgorgement. Musk's attorney Marc Toberoff said they plan to appeal to the Ninth Circuit.
curator_notes: Widely reported across 6+ outlets. Removes $150B litigation overhang and clears path for IPO filing 4 days later. Musk appeal keeps residual risk. Critical for IB audience.

headline: OpenAI and Dell Technologies Partner to Bring Codex to Hybrid and On-Premises Enterprise Environments
raw_snippet: OpenAI and Dell Technologies announced a multi-year collaboration to deploy Codex across hybrid and on-premises enterprise environments via the Dell AI Data Platform and Dell AI Factory. The deal is OpenAI's first explicit hybrid-and-on-prem enterprise distribution play, targeting financial services, healthcare, and government buyers that cannot send data to public cloud. Codex now has more than 4 million weekly developer users.
curator_notes: First on-prem enterprise distribution deal. Directly relevant to IB audience — regulated-industry AI adoption.

headline: OpenAI Becomes C2PA Conforming Generator and Integrates Google SynthID Watermarking for AI Content Provenance
raw_snippet: OpenAI became a C2PA Conforming Generator Product and integrated Google DeepMind's SynthID invisible watermarking into images generated by ChatGPT, Codex, and the API. SynthID embeds a pixel-level signal that survives screenshots and format changes. OpenAI also previewed a public verification tool that lets anyone check whether an image was generated using OpenAI tools.
curator_notes: Cross-industry collaboration with Google on content authenticity. Compliance/trust signal for regulated industries.

headline: OpenAI Model Disproves 80-Year-Old Erdős Conjecture in Discrete Geometry with 125-Page Proof
raw_snippet: An internal general-purpose reasoning model at OpenAI autonomously disproved a central conjecture in discrete geometry first posed by Paul Erdős in 1946 — the unit distance problem. The model produced a 125-page proof using algebraic number theory, identifying an infinite family of examples that provide a polynomial improvement over previous theories. The result was verified by external mathematicians who said 'AI has gone beyond being just an assistant.'
curator_notes: Milestone capability demonstration — general-purpose AI producing novel math proofs. Strengthens IPO narrative around reasoning capabilities.

Gartner recognized Codex's strengths across agentic software development, enterprise governance, sandboxing, and flexible deployment options. Codex is used by more than 4 million people weekly.

headline: ChatGPT Launches PowerPoint Add-In for AI-Powered Slide Creation and Editing
raw_snippet: OpenAI launched a ChatGPT add-in for Microsoft PowerPoint in beta, allowing users to create, edit, and update slides using AI-generated content. The add-in can ingest notes, documents, spreadsheets, images, and existing presentations. Available to all ChatGPT tiers including Free. Integrates with Outlook, Gmail, and SharePoint.
curator_notes: Deepens Microsoft Office integration. Available on all tiers. Direct relevance to IB audience.

headline: OpenAI Ships Codex to Mobile App and Chrome Extension
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced Codex now works on mobile (iOS and Android) and in Chrome. Users can monitor active AI workflows, approve commands, launch tasks, and supervise coding agents remotely. The mobile app uses a secure relay layer that keeps trusted machines reachable across devices. Available across all plans including Free and Go tiers.
curator_notes: Product extension — supports Codex adoption metrics ahead of IPO.
